note: 'No,” replied the king, “I insist on paying a price, for I will not offer to the LORD my God burnt offerings that cost me nothing.' (2Sam 24:24) -- fifty shekels of silver there, six hundred shekels of gold at 1Chr 21:25, which the two accounts do not reconcile and neither does this.

'And the plot of ground where he pitched his tent, he purchased from the sons of Hamor, Shechem’s father, for a hundred pieces of silver' (Gen 33:19). The parcel rather than the city; Joseph's bones were buried in it (Josh 24:32).

'So I bought the field in Anathoth from my cousin Hanamel, and I weighed out seventeen shekels of silver' (Jer 32:9) -- a field in a besieged country, bought as a sign that 'Houses, fields, and vineyards will again be bought in this land' (Jer 32:15).

'He bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver and built a city there, calling it Samaria after the name of Shemer, who had owned the hill.' (1Kgs 16:24). The city is named for the man who sold the ground.

The threshingfloor is his, and nearly the only thing the text tells us about him: 'the angel of the LORD was by the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite' (2Sam 24:16). Samuel spells him Araunah and Chronicles Ornan.
